feedback: If a bar doesn't start at zero or floats off the baseline, point out that height can only mean count when every bar starts at the same line; redraw from the baseline.

If a learner reads a value off by one, have them track the bar top straight across to the scale number and check whether they counted gridlines (including the baseline) instead of the value the top reaches.
If bars differ in width, ask what the extra width is supposed to represent; re-establish that only height carries the count, so widths must match.
activities.intendedInsight: Height means count: a bar's top read against the scale gives the number of items in that category. This only works if every bar starts from the shared zero baseline. Equal widths keep the bars fair to compare by eye, so that only height carries the count.
learnerActions: Collect or use a given data set with up to four categories (e.g. favourite pets: cats 9, dogs 6, fish 4, birds 2)
On squared/gridded paper or a gridded canvas, draw one bar per category, shading one square per unit so each bar's height equals its count
Keep every bar the same width, rising from a common baseline (zero line), evenly spaced, and label both axes with a single-unit scale
Read a chosen bar's value back by tracking its top straight across to the scale number, and check it matches the original count
activities.title: Build a bar graph from our data on gridded paper

feedback: If a learner answers 'how many more' with the taller bar's value (e.g. 9), align the two bars and count only the squares the taller one sticks up by; name that gap as 'how many more', then re-ask.
If they ask 'how did you get how many more?', check they computed a difference rather than simply reading a height.
For a put-together question, confirm they read both bar values and added them rather than reading one.
For a take-apart question, confirm they read the known part against the scale and took it away from the given total (e.g. 15 − 9 = 6), then checked the result against the other bar.
activities.intendedInsight: A comparison answer is the difference between two bars (the gap at the top), not the height of the taller bar; put-together and take-apart questions use the same read-the-scale skill with addition or subtraction.
learnerActions: On a finished bar graph, pick two categories and state a comparison question, e.g. 'how many more children chose cats than dogs?'
Line the two bars up side by side and count the squares by which the taller bar sticks up above the shorter one
Write the answer as a subtraction, e.g. cats 9 − dogs 6 = 3, and say in words that 3 is 'how many more'

Repeat with a put-together question ('how many chose cats and dogs together?') and a take-apart question ('15 children chose cats or dogs; use the cats bar to find how many of them did NOT choose cats, then check with the dogs bar') to practise combining and separating counts
activities.title: 'How many more' as the gap between two bars

feedback: If symbols vary in size or rows aren't aligned, ask whether a longer-but-fewer row could look bigger; redraw with equal, aligned symbols.
If a learner gives the longer row's total for 'how many more', line the rows up and count only the extra symbols; name that as the difference, then re-ask.
If a learner miscounts, have them count one symbol per unit and check the total against the data table.
activities.intendedInsight: Symbols must be uniform and aligned so that a row's length faithfully represents its count; 'how many more' is still the difference between the two counts, read as the extra symbols in the longer row.
learnerActions: Represent the same data as a picture graph, placing exactly one equal-sized symbol per unit in each category's row
Align symbols in rows so the length of a row can be compared at a glance

Read a category's count by counting its symbols, and answer a 'how many more' question by lining up the two rows and counting only the EXTRA symbols in the longer row (the difference, not the longer row's total)
Discuss what goes wrong if symbols are different sizes or not lined up
activities.title: Picture graph with uniform, aligned symbols
